title: Silicon interposer size and cost limits
bottleneck: 2.5D integration relies on silicon interposers, but reticle limits cap interposer size (~800 mm2 class), forcing multi-interposer stitching for the largest AI packages. Large interposers are expensive, fragile, and low-yield, and through-interposer vias add cost. Alternatives like organic or glass interposers trade electrical performance for size and cost.
why_it_blocks: Interposer limits cap how many chiplets can be integrated at high bandwidth, constraining the largest AI accelerators. The industry's main disaggregation vehicle is itself hitting scaling walls.
current_state: Large-body interposers and interposer-stitching are in production for flagship AI chips. Glass and organic alternatives are advancing but not yet performance-equivalent. Stitching multiple interposers adds assembly steps and failure points, raising cost exactly where disaggregation was supposed to save it.
